constraints: a single power of one variable; integer exponents 2-8; the answer is that exponent times the logarithm
hints: Identify the exponent on the argument as the coefficient that the power rule moves in front of the logarithm.
Apply log base a of x to a power equals that power times log base a of x, keeping the base unchanged.
Write the result as one logarithm multiplied by the original integer exponent.

objective: Logs of powers of the base
constraints: the argument is a power of the base itself; integer exponents 2-8; the answer is that exponent
hints: Recognize the argument as the stated logarithm base raised to a known power.
Use the power rule to bring that exponent outside the logarithm.
The remaining logarithm of the base equals one, so simplify to the exponent rather than expanding unrelated terms.

constraints: products, quotients and powers of two or three variables; integer exponents 2-3; expand fully into single-variable logarithms
hints: Break a logarithm of a product into a sum, and a logarithm of a quotient into a difference.
Apply the power rule to every variable power after separating the product or quotient.
Keep each final logarithm to one variable and preserve the signs from any denominator.

constraints: two or three logarithm terms sharing one base; integer coefficients 2-3; the answer is a single logarithm
hints: Move each numerical coefficient inside its logarithm as an exponent before combining terms.
Added logarithms combine as a product, while a subtracted logarithm becomes a denominator.
Write the resulting product-over-quotient as one logarithm with the common base.

constraints: express targets in terms of m = log_b 2 and n = log_b 3 (or similar)
hints: Rewrite the target number using the supplied factors whose logarithms are known.
Use the product, quotient, or power rule that matches that factorization.
Substitute the named log values only after the expression has been rewritten in terms of them.

constraints: the problem names the new base (common or natural); the answer is a quotient of two logarithms, left unevaluated
hints: The change-of-base formula uses the logarithm of the argument divided by the logarithm of the original base.
Use exactly the new base named in the question for both numerator and denominator.
Leave the quotient unevaluated, preserving the argument above and original base below.

constraints: numerator and denominator are logarithms of powers of one small integer; the answer is an exact integer or simple fraction
hints: Recognize the quotient as a change-of-base expression, even when it is written with natural logs.
Rewrite each logarithm of a power using the power rule.
Cancel the common logarithm of the underlying base and simplify the remaining numerical ratio.

objective: Solve by converting to exponential form
constraints: a single logarithm, already isolated; bases 2, 3, 4, 5; integer solutions
hints: A logarithmic equation states which exponent on the base produces its argument.
Rewrite the equation in exponential form, using the log argument as the positive result.
Evaluate that base power and confirm the resulting argument is positive.

constraints: two logarithms of the same base combined by the product or quotient rule; integer solutions, never at an excluded value
hints: Combine the same-base logarithms with the property named by their addition or subtraction.
After combining, use the one-to-one nature of logarithms to equate the positive arguments, or convert the single log equation to exponential form.
Solve the resulting ordinary equation and check that every original logarithm has a positive argument.

constraints: the right side is never an integer power of the base
hints: Because the right side is not a convenient power of the base, take the logarithm of both sides.
Use the power rule to bring the unknown exponent down as a multiplier.
Divide by the logarithm of the base and leave the exact quotient in the requested logarithm form.

constraints: an integer coefficient multiplies the exponential and is divided out first; what remains is an exact power of the base or an exact logarithm
hints: First isolate the exponential term by dividing away the numerical coefficient.
Check whether the isolated right side is a simple power of the base before choosing a logarithm method.
If logs are needed, take logs of both sides, use the power rule, and solve the resulting linear equation in the exponent.
